title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case rather than a model failure. The systems involved are law enforcement databases and camera systems, and the alleged misuse happened at the point of access, by a person with legitimate credentials using them for a purpose they were not granted for. The reported conduct includes tracking a woman without her consent and prohibited use of captured license plate data.

The controls that would catch this kind of conduct sit at the account and audit layer, not the model layer. Query logging, purpose checks, and review of lookups against the requester's assigned duties are the mechanisms that surface access that does not match a case. The reporting does not say which of these existed, which were reviewed, or when the conduct was first detected.

The charges are allegations from a grand jury indictment, and an indictment is not a finding of guilt. The reporting does not establish Rozar's intent, whether any data was retained or shared, or what the internal inquiry found.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff’s deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Prosecutors allege Rozar misused law enforcement databases and camera systems for personal reasons between April and May 2024, including tracking a woman without her consent.

The woman, who asked to remain anonymous, said she hopes speaking out encourages other women to report abuse. Rozar was terminated when the Georgia Bureau of Investigation began its inquiry, which former Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested in 2024. He was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. His arraignment is scheduled for May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
